caption.instagram:
You plan fewer than 183 days abroad. Does that settle where you owe tax?

Not on its own. Spending more than 183 days in a country is a common starting test for tax residency, and staying under it can avoid that one test. Many countries add others: a home there, work, family, where your life is centred, or days averaged over several years. A few months somewhere does not necessarily change residency; a long lease, local registration and 200 days often does.

Treaties between countries stop most income being taxed twice in full, but only when claimed correctly, and some countries tax unrealised gains when you leave. Tax can reduce or remove the saving from a move, depending on the two countries and the kind of income.
